recommendation: Keep the commit as-is because it fills the remaining conformance and guidance gaps without reversing later R6 changes. Treat FHIR-40256 and any richer composite-measure example work as separate follow-up if desired.
issue_request: FHIR-40422 was Applied/Persuasive for R5 and requested group-level Measure subject support, Measure.group.library/rateAggregation, MeasureReport.group.subject, exclusivity invariants for root-vs-group use, overview guidance, multi-subject updates for $evaluate-measure/$collect-data/$care-gaps, and related composite-measure context alignment.
initial_application: Commit c35d5cc2cf2596d936c47abfbe37c538a8abaa85 added the group-level Measure elements and MeasureReport.group.subject, and current Measure.library is already 0..*. The initial application did not update invariants, operations, or stale single-library guidance.

FHIR-49945 later listed FHIR-40422 as still needing application. No Zulip or Confluence search result changed the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published a source-changing commit that adds mea-9/mea-10/mea-11 constraints, updates Measure overview and quality-reporting logic guidance, and changes subject/subjectGroup cardinalities and documentation for $evaluate, $evaluate-measure, $collect-data, and $care-gaps to support multiple subject inputs with the Jira-specified individual/population restrictions.

source/measure/operationdefinition-Measure-evaluate.xml and source/measure/operationdefinition-Measure-evaluate-measure.xml: allowed multiple subject inputs and aligned reportType/default documentation with individual vs population modes.

source/measure/operationdefinition-Measure-collect-data.xml and source/measure/operationdefinition-Measure-care-gaps.xml: allowed multiple subject/subjectGroup inputs and documented one-per-type/profile individual/population restrictions.
source/measure/measure-introduction.xml and source/clinicalreasoning-quality-reporting.html: documented measure-level vs group-level declarations and removed stale single-library guidance.
